name: Olivier Chastel - Proposition de résolution (ensemble du texte)
title: REPORT on the proposal for a decision of the European Parliament and of the Council on the mobilisation of the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund for Displaced Workers following an application from Germany – EGF/2025/002 DE/Goodyear 2
part_text:
The European Parliament approves giving Germany 3,085,166 euros from the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund. The money helps 915 workers who lost their jobs when tyre maker Goodyear closed its Fulda plant and cut jobs in Hanau. It pays for retraining, job-search help, advice on starting a business, and digital skills courses. The fund covers 60 percent of the 5,141,944 euro total cost; Germany pays the rest. Most of the workers are over 50 or have low qualifications, so they need extra support.

- Germany receives 3.09 million euros to help 915 former Goodyear workers find new jobs.
- The money pays for retraining, job-search help, business advice and digital skills courses.
- Germany pays the remaining 40 percent; support runs from 1 November 2024 for up to 24 months.
